name: Curaçao
dek: Hato International Airport, WMO 78988. A country in the Kingdom of the Netherlands.
paragraphs: Curaçao is a constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands; this is its own sheet, as Aruba already is. The reference station is Curaçao Hato International Airport, WMO 78988, height 9 m. The same folder also has Princess Juliana Airport on Sint Maarten, which was not used. The IEC list still names the Netherlands Antilles rather than Curaçao, and no official driving-side or tipping page was opened on this pass, so the driving and tipping lines are missing.

The highest average high in the table is 33.0 °C, in September. The lowest average low is 24.5 °C, in January. The wettest month by the precipitation column is November, at 141.0 mm, and the driest is May, at 15.3 mm.

climate.caption: Reference station: Curaçao Hato International Airport, WMO 78988. Princess Juliana (Sint Maarten) is in the same folder and was not used.
climate.note: World Meteorological Organization 1991–2020 climatological standard normals, distributed by NOAA NCEI. Monthly values are copied as printed, with leading spaces removed; a value printed with no leading zero, such as -.3, is shown as -0.3.
climate.sourceTitle: WMO climate normals 1991-2020, Curaçao Hato International Airport (78988)

season: The National Hurricane Center says the Atlantic hurricane season runs from 1 June to 30 November.
The same page says the Atlantic basin includes the North Atlantic Ocean, the Caribbean Sea, and the Gulf of Mexico.

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type A, B, C and F, 127 V and 220 V, 50 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list, in the copy archived on 16 August 2026, shows the Netherlands Antilles at the voltage, frequency, and plug types in the figure. A direct download of the live page did not return the list, so the archive is the copy that was read. The archived list has no Curaçao row; it still uses the name Netherlands Antilles, of which Curaçao was a part until 2010. Aruba is listed separately on the same page and was not used here.

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Curaçao, last reviewed August 25, 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination, that standards may also differ within a country, and that risk may change depending on the activity. It points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217, in the list published 17 September 2026, lists the currency name Caribbean Guilder and the code XCG for Curaçao, and the same currency for Sint Maarten (Dutch part). It does not list the Netherlands Antillean Guilder for Curaçao in this edition.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone.tab gives Curaçao one row, America/Curacao. zone1970.tab lists that zone on a row named America/Puerto_Rico, which it shares with a long list of other Caribbean and Atlantic places. The backward file links America/Curacao to America/Puerto_Rico. The sheet prints the zone.tab name.

entry.label: Official entry requirements
entry.note: The official government site of Curaçao. We do not restate a visa rule.
